Rules

The boss. The Hamiltonian boss carries an energy shield. Its card shows the live estimate of ⟨H⟩ from your stream of shots: the dot is the estimate, the whisker is ±3σ (shot noise) and the red line is the shield. It falls in either of two ways. The live shots can prove ⟨H⟩ is below the shield: the estimate plus 3σ must be under the shield, with at least 10 shots per basis. That is about 99.7% confidence, and the estimate resets whenever you change the circuit. Each register carries 6 shots in level a and 200 in level b, where every shot is noisier, so a good state wins in about 5 to 6 registers. A state just under the shield needs many more shots; use the duel. Or an energy duel, an estimate from 8000 shots at once, can come out below the shield. A failed duel lets it surge forward. It shoves through the measurement gate (2 HP) and costs 3 base HP if it reaches the base, then comes back.

Shots, as in VQE. Every register is a volley of shots of your circuit (6 in level a, 200 in level b), like a small backend job; the lanes show its first outcome and its tag shows the average shot energy. Every term of H is made of X's only or Z's only, so two measurement settings are enough: X basis (H on every qubit, then measure) for the X·X terms, Z basis for the Z terms. A shot's energy is the sum of its terms, each ±1 times its coefficient. ⟨H⟩ is the sum of the two groups' averages, and the ± is one standard error: shot noise.

Level a: commuting ladder. H = X₀X₁ + X₁X₂ (the brief's X₁X₂ + X₂X₃, with Qiskit's 0-based labels). The ground energy is −2, reached when neighbours point opposite ways along x: |+−+⟩ or |−+−⟩. The planted Trotter step RXX(φ)·RXX(φ) = e^(−iφH/2) cannot change ⟨H⟩: time evolution conserves the energy of the Hamiltonian that generates it.

Level b: Trotter–Suzuki. A transverse field ½(Z₀+Z₁+Z₂) no longer commutes with the X·X terms. Start in |111⟩, the ground state of the field alone, and evolve under H(s) = s(X₀X₁+X₁X₂) + (1 − s/2)ΣZ as s goes from 0 to 1 over time T. If T is too short the state cannot follow the ground state (adiabatic theorem). Each step e^(−iAΔt)e^(−iBΔt) is only approximately e^(−i(A+B)Δt), with error O(Δt²) per step for 1st order; the symmetric 2nd-order Suzuki step e^(−iAΔt/2)e^(−iBΔt)e^(−iAΔt/2) cuts it to O(Δt³). Too few steps and the Trotter error wins. The ground energy is −2.403 and the shield sits at −2.20.

Game over when the base loses all 10 HP.
